newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court hits Karl Lagerfeld with big tax bill.
newsitem.headline: French court hits Karl Lagerfeld with big tax bill.

text.p: An administrative court in the Riviera resort of Nice slapped a huge tax bill on leading German fashion designer Karl Lagerfeld, concluding he evaded taxes during 1982-84, justice sources said on Monday.

They said the court, in a non-public judgment, ordered Lagerfeld to pay 18 million francs ($3.1 million) in back taxes after rejecting his argument that he was a resident of Monaco, whose residents are exempt from income tax.
Lagerfeld, chief designer for French fashion house Chanel, Italian firm Fendi and his own signature line, is one of the world's best-known fashion names.
During the June 4 trial, Lagerfeld's lawyer had argued that his client was a German national living in Monaco and therefore was not subject to French taxation.
But the state prosecutor argued that he was subject to French taxes because he had several French bank accounts, rented an apartment in Paris and owned property in Brittany.
The fact that Lagerfeld has lived in Monaco since 1982 did not prove he was a permanent resident there, the prosecutor said.
The ruling covers taxes due plus penalties for late payment, but does not include penalties for bad faith, the sources said.
